storyboard.claim: One candidate frames hardship as an enduring moral decay infecting every institution.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A stern candidate speaking grimly at a debate lectern.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivoting from sales to presidential debates.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts a grim, severe face on the candidate voicing permanent, pervasive decay.

storyboard.claim: The competing candidate frames the crisis as a temporary, specific hurdle to overcome together.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An upbeat candidate addressing voters with composed confidence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasting the pessimist's doom with the optimist's localized framing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the contrasting optimistic delivery directly facing the viewer.

storyboard.claim: Voters face an implicit statistical choice between explanatory styles in the voting booth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A voter poised at the voting lever deciding their choice.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Posing the decisive voter question after both candidate pitches.
storyboard.addedInformation: Grounds the statistical question in the physical act of pulling a ballot lever.

storyboard.claim: Historically, voters overwhelmingly choose the optimist, but testing candidates directly was impossible.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seligman in his office explaining the historical voting trend and scientific hurdle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answering the voting booth question with empirical history.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the methodological challenge of measuring psychology without questionnaire access.

storyboard.claim: Seligman's team bypassed testing candidates by inventing CAVE: Content Analysis of Verbatim Explanations.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seligman holding analysis transcripts in the university lab.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Solving the deadlock of testing public figures with a new method.
storyboard.addedInformation: The held transcript sheets show the exact textual medium being scored.

storyboard.claim: Researchers realized candidates leave an exhaustive record of explanations in public speeches.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seligman examining public speech archives in the university library.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explaining the core insight behind verbatim content analysis.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shifts attention from invasive testing to archival speech analysis.

storyboard.claim: The team extracted every causal statement explaining why good or bad events occurred.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seligman pointing to extracted causal statements on a lab board.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Detailing the extraction step of the CAVE protocol.
storyboard.addedInformation: Highlights the systematic rigor of cataloging all causal speech.

storyboard.claim: Statements were coded across permanence, pervasiveness, and personalization spanning elections from 1900 to 1984.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A structured three-bucket sorter diagram classifying explanatory dimensions.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Categorizing the extracted statements into Seligman's core dimensions.
storyboard.addedInformation: Maps out the three analytical buckets used to evaluate nearly a century of campaign rhetoric.

storyboard.claim: In 18 of 22 presidential elections, the more optimistic candidate overwhelmingly won.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The victorious optimistic candidate celebrating on the victory stage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Revealing the quantitative outcome of the historical election study.
storyboard.addedInformation: Presents the lopsided historical win rate visually through electoral celebration.

storyboard.claim: Electorates gravitate toward leaders who frame hardship as temporary and localized.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A resilient leader walking forward toward an open horizon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explaining why voters respond to this specific cognitive profile.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the forward-moving posture that optimistic framing projects to others.

storyboard.claim: Researchers expanded CAVE analysis to professional sports quotes, starting with the 1985 Mets.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host introducing the sports domain analysis with postgame press quotes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extending the explanatory model from presidential campaigns into athletic competition.
storyboard.addedInformation: Transitions the narrative smoothly from politics to baseball locker rooms.

storyboard.claim: The Mets framed losses as isolated oddities, blaming shifting wind or a one-off rotation blip.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A ballplayer shrugging off a loss at a postgame press microphone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Giving concrete quotes of temporary and external sports explanations.
storyboard.addedInformation: Captures the casual resilience of attributing defeat to transient conditions.

storyboard.claim: The more talented Cardinals expressed pervasive despair, stating the whole team was falling apart.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A dejected player slumping on the bench in defeat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasting the Mets' resilience with the Cardinals' catastrophic statements.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visualizes the physical deflation that accompanies pervasive explanations.

storyboard.claim: Teams with optimistic explanatory styles consistently outperformed betting spreads after setbacks.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seligman pointing to subsequent bounce-back performance data.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Demonstrating the tangible performance dividend of optimistic postgame quotes.
storyboard.addedInformation: Connects verbal explanatory habits directly to subsequent competitive rebound.

storyboard.claim: The definitive controlled sports experiment was conducted with Olympic champion Matt Biondi.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Matt Biondi standing focused beside the Olympic swimming lane.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introducing the premier controlled individual test in sports psychology.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places Biondi beside the signature swimming pool icon.

storyboard.claim: Researchers and his coach had Biondi swim a timed event giving his maximum possible effort.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Biondi stepping up to the starting blocks at the swimming lane.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Setting the baseline conditions for the experiment.
storyboard.addedInformation: Emphasizes the peak athletic exertion required before the experimental intervention.

storyboard.claim: When he finished, researchers deliberately deceived him with a falsely deflated time.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Biondi staring in shock at a stopwatch showing a deceptive time.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Delivering the deceptive experimental manipulation upon touching the wall.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Biondi's surprise when confronted with fabricated negative feedback.

storyboard.claim: The simulated failure was engineered to provoke his explanatory style before re-swimming.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seligman and Biondi discussing the protocol during the rest period.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explaining the scientific purpose of the artificial failure condition.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the trial as a psychological stress test before heat two.

storyboard.claim: When pessimistic swimmers were given fake bad times, they collapsed into helplessness and swam slower.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A deflated swimmer slumping by the bench, completely drained of morale.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Showing how pessimistic athletes reacted to the same false feedback.
storyboard.addedInformation: Demonstrates the performance drop caused by assuming failure is permanent.

storyboard.claim: Biondi, however, had tested as an extreme optimist on explanatory metrics.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Biondi standing upright and confident before his second swim.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasting the pessimistic swimmers' defeat with Biondi's psychological baseline.
storyboard.addedInformation: Presents Biondi's steadfast composure under adversity.

storyboard.claim: Instead of despairing, Biondi became energized and swam his second heat faster than his baseline.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Biondi celebrating triumphantly with a trophy in hand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Delivering the climax of the swimming resilience experiment.
storyboard.addedInformation: Celebrates the counter-intuitive speed improvement triggered by perceived failure.

storyboard.claim: The host challenges whether winning politicians sound optimistic merely because they lead in polls.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host speaking critically, questioning the direction of causality.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Raising a sharp methodological objection to the political election findings.
storyboard.addedInformation: Articulates the skeptic's core concern about poll-driven optimism.

storyboard.claim: It is effortless to sound hopeful when internal polling already grants a ten-point lead.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A complacent campaign manager smiling smugly over comfortable poll margins.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Elaborating the mechanism of how winning breeds cheerfulness.
storyboard.addedInformation: Draws the comfortable, unearned swagger of a front-runner.

storyboard.claim: A candidate trailing by double digits naturally turns grim and talks about fundamental crisis.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A trailing campaign worker slumping anxiously over grim poll numbers.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describing the opposing scenario where losing induces pessimism.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the mounting stress and defeatism of a sinking campaign.

storyboard.claim: Seligman's team controlled for polling leads, citing underdogs Harry Truman and JFK.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seligman calmly answering the critique with historical control cases.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rebutting the correlation challenge with rigorous historical data.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes that early optimistic rhetoric preceded voter support.

storyboard.claim: Both Truman and Kennedy began their national campaigns trailing significantly behind in the polls.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An underdog candidate campaigning resolutely against poor poll projections.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Providing concrete proof of candidates who were behind yet optimistic.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows determined campaigning despite adverse public predictions.

storyboard.claim: Truman faced unanimous expert predictions of a certain, humiliating defeat.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A candidate sitting determined at his desk amidst dire newspaper predictions.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Recalling the historic consensus that Truman had zero chance of winning.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strikes through the supposed inevitability of Truman's failure.

storyboard.claim: CAVE analysis showed Truman and Kennedy's explanatory style was far more optimistic than their opponents.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seligman holding the coded speech scores revealing the underdog's optimism.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Citing the quantitative speech metric (PESUM) that predicted the upset.
storyboard.addedInformation: Proves the speeches were optimistic long before poll numbers shifted.

storyboard.claim: The explanatory habit precedes the victory rather than merely reflecting it as a byproduct.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A leader striding purposefully toward the horizon before the race is decided.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarizing the causal arrow: explanatory style drives the win.
storyboard.addedInformation: Affirms that resilient cognitive habit is the cause, not the consequence.

storyboard.claim: The optimist campaigns harder, shrugs off bad press, and transmits resilience to voters.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A candidate holding an active protective shield while addressing voters.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describing the behavioral feedback loop that carries an underdog over the top.
storyboard.addedInformation: Uses the shield icon to signify cognitive protection against public attacks.

storyboard.claim: Having proven explanatory style in sales, sports, and politics, the discussion turns to the physical body.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host leaning forward to introduce the biological health research.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closing the competitive performance chapter and opening the health domain.
storyboard.addedInformation: Signals the thematic pivot into medical and biological stakes.

storyboard.claim: The discussion turns to physical health, immune resilience, and overall longevity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host presenting beside a symbolic heart icon representing vitality.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Setting the agenda for the physiological cost of explanatory style.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visualizes cardiovascular and systemic bodily health.

storyboard.claim: A devastating breakup inflicts an emotional toll, followed three weeks later by severe illness.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Elizabeth sitting despondent on the edge of the bed after a relationship ends.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introducing a concrete clinical scenario connecting emotional grief to sickness.
storyboard.addedInformation: Grounds the mind-body connection in everyday emotional trauma.

storyboard.claim: Bedridden and feverish with aching joints, catastrophic self-talk begins taking over.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Elizabeth lying awake in bed, visibly sick and staring at the ceiling.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Depicting the onset of severe flu three weeks after emotional distress.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the patient physically immobilized as negative thoughts loop.

storyboard.claim: Catastrophic internal dialogue laments having completely collapsed defenses.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Elizabeth brooding in bed, overwhelmed by helpless thoughts.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Quoting the exact pessimistic rumination during physical illness.
storyboard.addedInformation: Captures the subjective belief that the body has surrendered completely.

storyboard.claim: Illness following despair is not bad luck; mind and body separation is a total myth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seligman in a clinical setting dispelling the Cartesian divide.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reframing the illness from coincidence to biological consequence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strikes through the false belief that physical sickness is pure bad luck.

storyboard.claim: Chronic pessimism suppresses T-cell proliferation and cripples natural killer cell activity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seligman pointing toward clinical cellular immune metrics.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Detailing the specific physiological cascades triggered by chronic helplessness.
storyboard.addedInformation: Pairs the medical cross icon with specific immune system suppression.

storyboard.claim: Prolonged cortisol elevation increases cardiovascular strain and damages health over time.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seligman indicating persistent cardiovascular strain beside a heart icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extending immune impairment to long-term cardiovascular risks.
storyboard.addedInformation: Highlights the toll of chronic elevated cortisol on heart function.

storyboard.claim: Epidemiology confirms pessimism shortens life, proven definitively in Madelon Visintainer's rat tumor research.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seligman introducing the pivotal animal tumor study in the laboratory.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transitioning from human correlations to controlled oncology trials.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes the empirical landmark that linked helplessness to tumor progression.

storyboard.claim: Rats implanted with calibrated tumor cells were divided into control, escapable, and inescapable shock groups.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seligman demonstrating the triadic experimental design beside the shuttle box chamber.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Detailing the experimental setup of Visintainer's tumor implantation study.
storyboard.addedInformation: Uses the signature shuttle box icon representing the three-condition shock paradigm.
